main_text.p: Qui igitur mortem intempestivam & violentam sibi non vult attrahere, ille obnixè det operam, ut quantum in se est, omnia illa fugiat, quæ vim habent calidum & humidum nativum cum immi-nuendi tum corrumpendi.
main_text.head: CAPVT XVI. DE ANIMA VEGETANTE.
main_text.p: Anima vegetativa.Orpus autem animatum ut animatur per animam, ita & vivit per animam vegetantem & vigentem.

Est autem anima vegetans (quâ corpus animatum vivit: ἐντελέχεια corporis vegetabilis, quâ vegetabile, seu, actus primus naturalis organici corporis, quo illud vivit, nutrimento assumto nutritur, augetur, & simile sibi in specie gignit.
Dici potest anima vivifica qua corpus si-ta vivificatum vivit, & naturalis vitæ actiones edit.
Anima vegetantis facultates tres.Hujus facultates sunt tres, Altrix, Auctrix, Procreatrix.

page.notes: Left margin notes are catchwords: "Anima vegetativa." (upper) and "Anima vegetantis facultates tres." (lower); the lower one is set in small type and was copied as a single note. The Greek word ἐντελέχεια is printed as "ivλέχεια" in the scan and was transcribed with the closest Greek reading; treat with caution. "Orpus" is printed as shown (a large initial O joined to "rpus"; the initial appears as a woodcut ornament, so it is read as "Corpus" by the printer's convention and kept as printed where uncertain). Last line of the main text is a hyphenated word continuing to the next page.
